Published online:
    August 28, 2026

Geographic focus:
    United States (Jackson Hole, Wyoming — global central banking context)

Temporal focus:
    T1. Historical report [NO]
    T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [YES]
    T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [YES]

Synopsis:
    Fed Chair Kevin Warsh delivered his keynote at Jackson Hole, marking a hawkish pivot relative to his prior vague stance. He stopped short of explicit forward guidance but signaled the Fed has "work to do" if inflation doesn't credibly move toward 2%. PCE remains at 3.7% YoY as of July, with ~50% of the PCE basket still running above 3% annualized. Warsh acknowledged short-term rates are the primary policy tool, that financial conditions show little sign of restraint, and that credit markets are not tightening. Three FOMC members dissented at the July meeting in favor of a hike. Rate futures moved to ~60% probability of a September hike post-speech, up from 40%. The next key data — August jobs, unemployment, and CPI — drops early September ahead of the Sep 15–16 FOMC meeting.

Q01. Is the content relevant to US economy, US yields, US interest rates and US market pricing?
Relevance: YES — directly addresses Fed policy rate trajectory, inflation dynamics, financial conditions, and live market repricing of rate hike odds.

Q02. Is the content about increasing US interest rates?
Relevance: 85 (strongly yes — hawkish pivot, "work to do" language, 3 dissenters favoring hikes, market repricing higher)
Probability of increase: 60% (as priced by rate futures post-speech; Sep hike conditional on incoming August inflation data)

Q03. Is the content about holding stable US interest rates?
Relevance: 40 (yes, but receding — majority at July meeting still voted to hold and await data; one more inflation print before Sep decision)
Probability of holding: 40% (residual market pricing post-speech)

Q04. Is the content about decreasing US interest rates?
Relevance: 2 (virtually absent — cuts are not discussed; Trump's preference for lower rates is noted only as a political backdrop Warsh appears to be distancing himself from)
Probability of decrease: 0%

Q05. Focus on the very latest information: What is the sentiment/tone including the very latest information on US interest rates?
Sentiment: +65 (meaningfully more hawkish than before — clearest signal yet that hikes are on the table; shift from vague promises to conditional tightening language, market repricing confirms the hawkish read; tempered slightly by lack of explicit forward guidance and data dependency ahead of Sep meeting)
